scope.notes: Inventory in progress (283 rows). Covers Exalted: The Abyssals character-creation overview (Chapter Three), the universal Anima Effect available to every caste, all five Castes with their Anima Banners/Anima Effects/Caste Abilities/Associations, the Abyssal Curse, the Virtues of Death, the Resonance Trait (Abyssal Limit analog) including gain/loss/manifestation rules and the 1-10 Resonance Manipulation Effects table, the-title, Useful Crafts, the Cult-and-Abyssals exclusion sidebar, the six new deathknight-only Backgrounds (Abyssal Command, Liege, Necromancy, Spies, Underworld Manse, Whispers), the altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Backing/Mentor, Familiar, Followers, Manse), all 228 Chapter Five Charm rows (pp. 157-222, PDF 158-223) covering every Ability line for all five Castes, and now all of Chapter Six's Shadowlands (First) Circle (9 spells) and Labyrinth (Second) Circle (10 spells: Arisen Legion, Call the Greater Servitor, Rune of Sweet Passing's Labyrinth variant text, Exquisite Undead Aide, Hundred Shade Breath, Ivory Razor Forest, Reaping the Fallen, Blood from the Slaughter, Spiteful Passing, Stealing the Gathered Breath, Striking Spectre Lash), plus the start of the Void (Third) Circle (its section-heading row plus 7 spells so far: Abyssal Aegis, Anguished Shade Harvest, Blood Monsoon, Dimming of the Light, Inauspicious Citadel, Lord of the Dead, Poisoning the Well), printed pp. 224-230/PDF 225-231. One Moonshadow Linguistics row (Corpus-Rending Blow) is an explicit unresolved placeholder: it is referenced as a prerequisite by Ghost-Warding Glyph but no matching Charm write-up was found in the rendered pages.

sources.role: Primary Abyssal rules, Charms, Backgrounds, and setting material

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 1 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 1) for the copy used to build this inventory; both are recorded on every citation. Confirmed again at the Chapter Five Day Caste boundary: the rendered PDF page 201 shows printed folio '200' at the bottom, matching this offset.
This PDF is image-based (no selectable text layer); all rows below were transcribed from rendered page images, per the 'OCR is an extraction aid, never verification by itself' rule.
Abyssals do not have a Limit Trait; Resonance (1-10) fills the equivalent role and is tracked/gained/lost differently. See the resonance-* inventory rows.

A small number of Chapter Five rows have summary text (copied from the book's own prose) that labels more than one Charm as a tree 'capstone' within the same Ability line, most notably in the Dusk Caste Melee material around attunement-shattering-block/eye-of-the-tempest, and the Daybreak Caste Medicine sub-tree numbering jumps from 'second' to 'third' without an identified second sub-tree in this pass. The per-row citations and mechanical content are still accurate to their page, but the exact tree-branch topology in those spots needs a dedicated disambiguation review before this content is promoted to a production catalog.

The Day Caste Athletics 'Soaring Raptor Prana' row and the Larceny 'Striking Snake Grab' row are marked unreviewed: their headers, costs, and prerequisites were confirmed from the printed Charm tree and cross-references, but their full rules-text paragraphs were not legibly captured in this extraction pass and need a follow-up close read before promotion.

The Moonshadow Caste Linguistics tree's 'Ghost-Warding Glyph' lists 'Corpus-Rending Blow' as a prerequisite Charm, but no Charm write-up by that name was found anywhere in the rendered Chapter Five or Chapter Six pages. A placeholder row (id: corpus-rending-blow, disposition: unresolved) was added so the gap is tracked explicitly rather than silently dropped; do not promote Ghost-Warding Glyph until this is resolved.

Chapter Six's necromancy framework references 'the appropriate Charm' gating each circle (paralleling Terrestrial/Celestial/Solar Circle Sorcery), but no such Charm was found as its own stat block in the rendered pages -- it may be presented differently than standard sorcery-access Charms, or on a page not yet rendered. The 'necromancy-framework-and-circles' reference-only row and all 9 Shadowlands Circle spell rows are marked unreviewed/reviewed as captured, but this gating mechanism needs follow-up before the necromancy system is promotable.

Only the Shadowlands (First) Circle of necromancy has been inventoried so far. The Labyrinth (Second) Circle and Void (Third) Circle spell lists remain in Chapter Six, past printed p. 227/PDF 228, and are not yet located/rendered.

The Labyrinth (Second) Circle (10 spells, printed pp. 224-228/PDF 225-229) is now fully inventoried: Arisen Legion and Call the Greater Servitor (two named variants of the Labyrinth-level Raise the Skeletal Horde upgrade, each with distinct mote costs and effects), a Labyrinth-Circle continuation of Rune of Sweet Passing, Exquisite Undead Aide, Hundred Shade Breath, Ivory Razor Forest, Reaping the Fallen, Blood from the Slaughter, Spiteful Passing, Stealing the Gathered Breath, and Striking Spectre Lash. The Void (Third) Circle then begins at printed p. 228/PDF 229 with its own section-heading row (the-void-circle, reference-only) followed by 7 spells so far: Abyssal Aegis, Anguished Shade Harvest, Blood Monsoon, Dimming of the Light, Inauspicious Citadel, Lord of the Dead, and Poisoning the Well (printed pp. 228-230/PDF 229-231). The per-circle gating Charms (shadowlands-circle-necromancy/labyrinth-circle-necromancy/void-circle-necromancy) were already inventoried in an earlier pass as part of the Daybreak Caste's Occult tree, resolving the open question in the earlier rulesNotes entry above about whether they existed as their own stat blocks. Resume point for the next round: printed p. 230/PDF 231, continuing the Void Circle spell list past Poisoning the Well.
